newsitem.title: BELGIUM: Luxembourg CLT-UFA says no plans to sell M6, TPS.
newsitem.headline: Luxembourg CLT-UFA says no plans to sell M6, TPS.

text.p: Luxembourg broadcast group CLT-UFA on Wednesday denied Tuesday's French newspaper report which said it might be about to unload its interests in French TV channel M6 and French digital broadcasting consortium TPS.

"In the eyes of Mr Remy Sautter, director general of CLT-UFA, the extremely positive results of these two companies represent guaranteed value in CLT-UFA's portfolio. Their sale is not envisaged," CLT-UFA said in a statement.
CLT-UFA is owned 50-50 by Luxembourg holding company Audiofina and German publisher Bertelsmann.

France's Le Figaro newspaper said on Tuesday that CLT-UFA might pull out of M6 and TPS as part of a wider plan by Belgian businessman Albert Frere to swap his control of Audiofina for a direct stake in French media group Havas.
Together, Frere and Havas control Audiofina through a separate holding company called CLMM. Frere's stake is held through Belgian holding company Electrafina.

CLT, which merged with Bertelsmann's UFA unit earlier this year, holds around 39.5 percent of M6 and has around a fifth of French digital television station Television Par Satellite (TPS) -- Brussels Newsroom +32 2 287 6810, Fax +32 2 230 7710
